_declaration: LD-11 block_fp8_linear numerics declaration (restated at port-plan iteration 5; AMENDED at author_kernel_triads iteration 3 -- see 'iteration3_restatement' below, which ADDS clauses and moves none). COMMITTED BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT: this file is committed first and the graded legs run over a scratch checkout at a later-or-equal commit, so scripts/triad_numerics.py leg 0 can prove mechanically that the thresholds predate the numbers they grade. Thresholds, shapes, cases and the timeout are transcribed from port-plan.md section 1(c) and port-assessment.md section 3.2; nothing here was chosen after seeing a result, and nothing here may be widened afterwards (plan section 6 records the alternative for a missed envelope: ladder row LD-25, plan-level, never a widened threshold).

iteration3_restatement._why: Iteration 2 graded 8 of 8 declared cases and passed, yet the NKI kernel DOES NOT COMPILE and the torch fallback DOES NOT LOWER. Both defects are invisible to the venues iteration 2 used -- the NKI CPU simulator does not enforce the ISA operator table, and eager torch never lowers to HLO. This amendment therefore adds (1) two arithmetic restatements with their own bit-exactness clauses and (2) TWO MANDATORY VENUES that make those two defect classes visible. NO ITERATION-2 CLAUSE IS CHANGED OR WIDENED. Iteration 2's conclusion that LD-11 was hardware-ready is SUPERSEDED IN PLACE by this block; its measured numbers stand.

finding_A_kernel_operator.defect: block_fp8_linear.py's NKI kernel issues nisa.tensor_scalar(op0=nl.divide) UNCONDITIONALLY in the activation-quantize step. The installed wheel rejects it: 'nki/isa/_tensor_ops.py:387: error: invalid kwarg op0: unsupported operator divide'. nl.divide exists as a SYMBOL, which is why the call reads as legal and why no import-time or simulator check caught it.
finding_A_kernel_operator.restatement: a_scale is ALWAYS the exact power of two 2**(f-127), where f is the ue8m0 ceil_field. Its reciprocal is therefore the exact power of two 2**(127-f), whose biased exponent field is 254-f. The kernel builds inv_a_scale by integer arithmetic on the field (op0=nl.multiply operand0=-1, op1=nl.add operand1=254, then op0=nl.left_shift operand0=23, then reinterpret) and MULTIPLIES by it. Every operator used is one the compiler admits.

clause_bit_exact_vs_divide._what: x * inv_a_scale must be BITWISE identical to x / a_scale at fp32 for every ceil_field the gate's envelope admits. Both are exact scalings by a power of two, so this is exact by IEEE-754 rather than by tolerance -- there is no threshold to widen here.
clause_bit_exact_vs_divide._declared_field_domain: The gate admits bf16 activations only. _AMAX_FLOOR/fp8_max = 4.166667e-07 gives ceil_field 106; bfloat16_max/fp8_max = 1.412305e+36 gives ceil_field 248. So ceil_field is in [106, 248] and inv_field = 254 - ceil_field is in [6, 148] -- every value a NORMAL fp32 exponent field, so neither a_scale nor its reciprocal is ever subnormal or infinite.
clause_bit_exact_vs_divide._why_not_nisa_reciprocal: nisa.reciprocal also compiles and is one instruction shorter, but it is a Vector-Engine instruction whose accuracy ON DEVICE cannot be observed from a device-free venue. Choosing it would move a numerics question to hardware that arithmetic settles here. Recorded, not selected.

finding_B_ceiling_restatement.defect: The ue8m0 power-of-two ceiling is computed by an IEEE-754 integer bit trick in TWO places -- block_fp8_linear.py's _pow2_ceil_scale and attention/mla_qkv.py's _round_scale_pow2, which the former's docstring declares to be a local copy that 'must stay identical'. Neither lowers through the production vllm_neuron/compile/hlo.py:convert_fx_to_hlo: 'aten.__rshift__.Scalar -> RuntimeError: Expected XLA tensor. Got: XLAIntType'. The mla_qkv copy is the harder blocker: mla_qkv.py has NO _can_use_* dispatch pair, and its call is guarded only by kv_nope_fp8_qat, which is passed explicitly True at both production call sites and defaults True, so it is traced unconditionally on the production path.
finding_B_ceiling_restatement.measured_venue_facts: Against a 2-input matmul control AND a 1-input fp32 elementwise control that both reach a NEFF, every crash retried once and DETERMINISTIC: mul/add, floor, ceil, log2, min/max, divide, pow, exp, clamp all COMPILE; the fp32->int32 bitcast SEGFAULTS (rc -11); torch.exp2 SEGFAULTS (rc -11); frexp and ldexp ABORT (rc -6); >>, bitwise_right_shift and int32 multiply FAIL to lower. So every bit-trick form, every frexp form and every exp2 form is unavailable on this venue.
finding_B_ceiling_restatement.restatement: s = pow(2.0, floor(log2(v))) as an EXACT power-of-two seed, then three EXACT fixups that remove log2's error entirely: halve while s > v; double while 2s <= v; then double unless s == v. Each selector is built from divide, floor/ceil and minimum/maximum on integer-valued or ratio quantities -- no boolean tensor, no bitcast, no int32 arithmetic. log2 only has to land within one binade, which it does by many orders of magnitude, so NONE of its error reaches the result.

clause_bit_exact_vs_incumbent._what: The restatement must be BITWISE identical to the incumbent bit trick over the whole declared domain, EXACT POWERS OF TWO INCLUDED. That is the crux, not a detail: mla_qkv.py:211's docstring records that at an exact power of two fp32 log2 can land a hair either side of the integer and flip the ceiling by ONE WHOLE EXPONENT of quantization error.
clause_bit_exact_vs_incumbent._domain_a: fp8_max = 1.0, so 1.0/fp8_max is exactly 1.0 and v == amax BITWISE. This is the ONLY way to place v exactly on a power of two, so it is how the crux is graded: exact powers of two 2**-40..2**40, both nextafter neighbours of each, _AMAX_FLOOR, 4096 uniform-random values, and three probes in every admitted binade 2**-30..2**30.
clause_bit_exact_vs_incumbent._domain_b: fp8_max = FP8_CLAMP_MAX (240.0): bf16 group amax across four magnitudes, amax chosen so v lands on a power of two, and the two extremes _AMAX_FLOOR and bfloat16_max.
clause_bit_exact_vs_incumbent._counter_example_measured_not_assumed: exp2(ceil(log2 v)) -- the obvious restatement -- was graded and is NOT bit-exact: 73 of 81 mismatches at nextafter-above-a-power-of-two, each off by exactly a factor of 0.5, i.e. one whole exponent. exp(k*ln2) is likewise NOT bit-exact (225 and 524 mismatches). Both are recorded as measured counter-examples so the selected form's exactness is a comparison, not a claim.
clause_bit_exact_vs_incumbent._declared_domain_boundary: v >= _AMAX_FLOOR/fp8_max = 4.166667e-07. amax is an absolute maximum clamped at _AMAX_FLOOR, so SUBNORMAL v cannot occur on any path this op has.
clause_bit_exact_vs_incumbent._declared_deviation_outside_that_boundar: For SUBNORMAL v the incumbent bit trick FLOORS at 2**-126 (its exponent field is 0, so ceil_log2 saturates at -126), while every non-bit form returns the true ceiling. Measured: 3 of 4 subnormal probes differ. This is DECLARED rather than absorbed, and it is outside the declared domain above, so it grades as a recorded deviation and never as a pass. No threshold is moved to accommodate it.

finding_B_ceiling_restatement.both_copies_in_scope: vllm_neuron/functional/block_fp8_linear.py:_pow2_ceil_scale AND vllm_neuron/functional/attention/mla_qkv.py:_round_scale_pow2. The mla_qkv copy is lead-granted into this triad's authoring surface (2026-08-19T13:24Z) on the grounds that block_fp8_linear.py:341 declares in-tree that the two are the same clause of the same recipe and must stay identical. _round_scale_pow2 has no declaration file of its own and is graded under THIS declaration as the shared helper. The two must remain bitwise-equal to each other, and that equality is itself a graded clause.
finding_B_ceiling_restatement.invariants_preserved: (a) F-7 route (i): fp8_max DEFAULTS to the platform-resolved FP8_CLAMP_MAX (240.0 on trn2), never the reference's literal 448. (b) The divisor in the scale and the clamp in the caller remain the SAME ceiling. Neither is touched by this restatement, and the LD-24 / legacy-grid encoding settlement of iteration 2 and F-7 is undisturbed.

finding_C_fp8_transpose._how_it_was_found: It was NOT found by reading code. Finding A's operator fix was applied and graded, and the whole in-tree kernel body STILL failed the mandatory compile venue below -- with the divide gone, the compiler reached the NEXT instruction and rejected that. This block is therefore added in the same iteration as findings A and B, before any code change for it, and it is the direct product of the venue this amendment made mandatory. A defect discovered only because a newly mandated venue was run is the venue justifying itself.
finding_C_fp8_transpose.defect: The kernel transposes both matmul operands with nisa.dma_transpose into a 1-BYTE (fp8) destination, and the installed wheel forbids that outright: "nki/isa/_transpose.py:640:9: error: 'nisa.dma_transpose' op 'dst' must be not a 1-byte or packed MX type (int8, uint8, float8, and packed MX x4 are excluded), got 'f8E4M3'". TWO sites, both required: block_fp8_linear.py:194 transposes the fp8 weight block ([n_sz, K_block] HBM -> [K_block, n_sz] SBUF) and block_fp8_linear.py:330 transposes the fp8-quantized activation block ([m_sz, K_block] SBUF -> [K_block, m_sz] SBUF). Neither is incidental: nisa.nc_matmul contracts on the PARTITION axis, so both operands must arrive with K on partitions. Invisible to iteration 2 for the same reason finding A was -- the NKI CPU simulator does not enforce the ISA/MLIR verifier, and dma_transpose is exact on 1-byte data THERE.
finding_C_fp8_transpose.measured_route_table: Every transpose route the wheel exposes, each compiled at the tile the kernel actually uses ([128,128] fp8) AND ending in a real nc_matmul that consumes the transposed tile, in BOTH orientations the kernel needs. Against a passing add/multiply control, and with the incumbent as a negative control that MUST still fail. WEIGHT site (HBM->SBUF): T0 incumbent fp8 dma_transpose FAILED (finding C reproduced); T1 the SAME call with a 2-BYTE dst COMPILED (so the rejection is the 1-byte width, not the call, the shapes or the harness); T2 fp8->bf16->dma_transpose->fp8 COMPILED; T3 nc_transpose fp8 SBUF -> fp8 PSUM on engine=tensor COMPILED; T3b nc_transpose with an SBUF dst FAILED ("Vector engine transpose requires shape <= [32, 32], got [128, 128]" -- an SBUF dst forces VectorE); T4 nl.load_transpose2d FAILED with the IDENTICAL dma_transpose diagnostic (it is a thin wrapper over the same op); T5 one dma_copy per output column COMPILED; T6 nl.transpose FAILED ("moving must be in [sbuf], got psum"). ACTIVATION site (SBUF->SBUF, where an HBM transposing load does not apply): A-T0 incumbent FAILED; A-T2 COMPILED; A-T3 COMPILED. So exactly TWO routes serve BOTH sites: T2 and T3.
finding_C_fp8_transpose.restatement: T2 AT BOTH SITES: widen the fp8 tile to bf16 with nisa.tensor_copy, dma_transpose in bf16 (2-byte dst, admitted), narrow back to fp8 with nisa.tensor_copy. The matmul operands stay fp8, so the matmul dtype, the ue8m0 scaling, and the LD-24 legacy-grid encoding settlement are all untouched -- only the transpose staging changes.
finding_C_fp8_transpose._why_T2_and_not_T3: The SAME pre-registered rule that selected finding A's K2 over nisa.reciprocal, applied consistently: prefer the route whose exactness follows from IEEE-754 over the route that rests on a device instruction's accuracy, which a device-free venue cannot observe. T2 is exact by representability: every finite float8_e4m3 value sits exactly in bfloat16 (4 exponent bits inside 8, 3 mantissa bits inside 7), so the widen and the narrow are both the IDENTITY on the fp8 grid and dma_transpose only moves bytes. T3's exactness rests on the wheel's own claim that "Starting NeuronCore-v3, all Tensor Engine transpose is bit-accurate" (trn2 is v3) -- which is credible, contradicts the kernel docstring's earlier reason for avoiding TensorE, and is still a vendor claim rather than a measurement available here. T3 IS RECORDED AS A COMPILING ALTERNATIVE with a real perf advantage, for a later perf rung with device evidence; it is not selected now. T5 compiles but issues one DMA descriptor per output column (128 per tile) and is recorded as clearly worse, not selected.
finding_C_fp8_transpose._what: In the NKI CPU simulator, the transposed fp8 tile the kernel produces must equal the plain transpose of the same fp8 codes, compared as RAW 1-BYTE CODES rather than as decoded floats, at both declared shapes and at both sites. Bytes, not floats: a float comparison would let a re-encoding between the OCP and legacy e4m3 grids pass unnoticed, and LD-24 is exactly about that distinction.
finding_C_fp8_transpose._end_to_end_clause_is_the_existing_one: The whole-op clauses are NOT restated and NOT widened. The five harness cases and the three encoding cases are re-run at the settling commit under the SAME thresholds iteration 2 used, and the transpose change must leave them passing. If the round trip were not the identity, the fp8 codes feeding every matmul would change and those clauses would fail -- so they are the end-to-end discriminator for this finding, with the byte clause above as its localization.
finding_C_fp8_transpose.perf_trade_recorded_not_hidden: T2 costs two extra tensor_copy instructions and one transient bf16 staging tile per transposed tile, at both sites. At the larger declared shape that is NB*KB = 64*8 = 512 weight tiles plus KB = 8 activation tiles per M tile. This is a PERF trade recorded for the perf report (the same way the one-128-wide-N-tile choice and the unsharded LNC-2 launch already are), never a correctness one, and it is NOT a reason to widen any clause. T3 is the recorded cheaper alternative if a later rung buys device evidence for it.
finding_C_fp8_transpose.invariants_preserved: The matmul still consumes fp8 operands; fp8_max still resolves to the platform FP8_CLAMP_MAX (240.0 on trn2, F-7 route (i)); the scale divisor and the clamp remain the same ceiling; the ue8m0 arithmetic and finding A's exact reciprocal are untouched; no threshold anywhere in this file is moved.

mandatory_venues._why: Iteration 2's venues were the NKI CPU simulator plus eager torch ONLY. The simulator does not enforce the ISA operator table and eager execution never lowers to HLO, which is exactly how a kernel that cannot compile and a fallback that cannot lower both passed 8 of 8. Simulator and eager numerics remain NECESSARY for the numerics clauses; they are no longer SUFFICIENT evidence of a working path.
mandatory_venues.kernel_compiles: Every NKI kernel body must compile through vllm_neuron.nki.nki_compile.compile_nki at both declared shapes (M=128 K=1024 N=1024, and M=512 K=1024 N=8192, the indexer's wq_b projection).
mandatory_venues.fallback_lowers: Every traceable torch fallback and every helper it calls must lower through the production vllm_neuron/compile/hlo.py:convert_fx_to_hlo.
mandatory_venues.control_required_in_the_same_run: Each venue leg must carry a PASSING control graph in the same run, so a broken harness is distinguishable from a real defect. For the HLO venue the controls are a 2-input fp32 matmul reaching a NEFF and a 1-input fp32 elementwise graph reaching a NEFF -- the single-input control matters, because a 2-input-only control cannot tell 'this op does not lower' from 'this harness cannot do elementwise graphs'. For the compile_nki venue the control is a minimal add/multiply kernel declared at MODULE level.
mandatory_venues.crash_isolation_required: Lowering can SEGFAULT or ABORT the interpreter (measured: rc -11 for the bitcast and for exp2, rc -6 for frexp/ldexp), which try/except cannot observe. Every lowering case must therefore run in its own subprocess and report the signal as its verdict, and a crash must be retried once so a transient blip is distinguishable from a deterministic verdict.

_venue: trn2-2, pinned venv /opt/aws_neuronx_venv_pytorch_inference_vllm_0_21_0_1_0_0, device-free. Every graded leg exports NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE=trn2 BEFORE the first import (R-24): FP8_CLAMP_MAX is frozen at import time and falls back to 448.0 in bare CPU mode, so a leg that imports first would grade against the wrong fp8 ceiling and pass for the wrong reason.
_two_instruments: The plan declares EIGHT cases. Five are expressible in this harness's input vocabulary (shape/dtype/kind/seed) and are graded here. THREE are the encoding cases added at iteration 5; they require weight bytes that were exponent-field 15 in the checkpoint's OCP grid and their paired doubled block scale, i.e. the actual output of the LD-24 loader transforms. The harness can generate only randn/rand/ones/zeros/arange/randint inputs, so it cannot construct them: they are declared under 'supplementary_cases' below and graded by the committed probe artifacts/repairs/author_kernel_triads-iter2/probe_ld11_triad.py, which runs the SAME two legs with the SAME env discipline (fallback: VLLM_NEURON_CPU_MODE=1 + VLLM_NEURON_DISABLE_NKI_KERNELS=1; simulator: VLLM_NEURON_CPU_MODE=1 + NKI_SIMULATOR=1) against the SAME plain-torch reference and reads its thresholds from THIS file. Neither instrument invents a threshold; the split is a limit of the harness's input vocabulary, recorded rather than absorbed.

reference._why: Plain torch, outside the port package (the harness refuses a reference resolving inside vllm_neuron). Written in the scaled-partial form while the triad's fallback is written in the dequantize-then-matmul form, so leg 1 compares two independent spellings of the declared math.

_tolerance_derivation.compared_quantity: the op's returned tensor at the contract's default out_dtype=torch.bfloat16 (the harness upcasts both sides to fp32 before comparing, so equal bf16 values compare equal).
_tolerance_derivation.rtol: 2**-7 = 0.0078125. bf16 carries 7 stored mantissa bits, so for a value v in [2**e, 2**(e+1)) one ULP is 2**(e-7) and one ULP RELATIVE lies in (2**-8, 2**-7]. rtol = 2**-7 is therefore the smallest relative tolerance that admits ANY single-ULP difference wherever it falls in a binade, which is exactly the declared clause 'bf16 output exact except positions differing by exactly one bf16 ULP'. It is four orders of magnitude below every defect class this gate exists to catch (a transposed weight, a swapped scale index, a wrong group boundary, a mis-sharded scale grid each move the output by >= 100%).
_tolerance_derivation.atol: 0.0. An absolute floor would let a near-zero output disagree by many ULPs unnoticed; the relative clause is the declared one.
_tolerance_derivation.not_a_substitute: allclose(rtol=2**-7) admits a one-ULP difference at EVERY position. The declared clause also CAPS the number of such positions at 0.1%, and caps non-finite outputs at 0, and bounds the pre-cast fp32 accumulator at 2e-05 max_rel. Those three counted/measured clauses are below under 'clauses' and are graded by the committed probe, which reads them from here. A pass on this harness alone does not settle them.

clauses._basis: port-plan.md section 1(c) / port-assessment.md section 3.2, verbatim. non-finite cap 0 is the defect this replan exists to kill (32/1024 -> 0/1024, legs E1 vs E2b of artifacts/repairs/author_kernel_triads-iter1/). 2e-05 sits ~15x above the measured 1.32114e-06 for the LD-24 halving at one 128-contraction block and four orders below any real defect class.
clauses._measured_on: fp32_accumulator_max_rel is measured with the op called at out_dtype=torch.float32 (the pre-cast accumulator the clause names); the bf16 clauses are measured at the contract default out_dtype=torch.bfloat16.

cases.name: cte_m4096_k4096_n1536
cases._role: plan case 1 of 5: the CTE prefill shape, fused_wqa_wkv at TP=64.
cases._simulator_note: Declared true deliberately. 32 x 12 x 32 tiled matmuls through the numpy simulator may exceed the declared 1200s timeout, in which case the harness records UNCOVERED - loudly, never as a pass - and hardware proof for this shape stays with compile_and_serve. Declaring it false would have hidden the question.

cases.name: tkg_m64_k1024_n512
cases._role: plan case 2 of 5: the TKG decode shape (R-8's least favourable shape for a PE-array fp8 matmul).

cases.name: sub_block_n_shard_n64
cases._role: plan case 3 of 5: a sub-block-N shard. N=64 < block_n=128, one grid row shared by the cores that split it (weight_loaders._grid_shard). The kernel must not assume N is a whole number of 128-blocks.

cases.name: exactly_one_k_block_k128
cases._role: plan case 4 of 5: K_local = 128 exactly - one contraction block, one activation group, a [N/128, 1] scale grid. The degenerate loop bound.

cases.name: out_of_envelope_fp32_activations
cases._role: plan case 5 of 5: the out-of-envelope case that MUST take the fallback. x is fp32; the kernel envelope admits bf16 activations only, so _can_use_block_fp8_linear returns False and the same call site runs the torch fallback on both legs. What it proves is that the gate REJECTS: the simulator leg's agreement is trivial by construction, and the probe additionally records the gate's boolean verdict per case so the rejection is evidence rather than an inference.

supplementary_cases.name: encoding_field15_preimage_block
supplementary_cases._role: plan encoding case 1 of 3: a weight block holding at least one byte that carried exponent field 15 in the checkpoint's OCP grid - the case that produced 32/1024 non-finite outputs unremedied (leg E1). Built by drawing a block under the checkpoint's own recipe (ue8m0 power-of-two block scale against OCP 448, clamp +-448) until a field-15 byte appears, then passing the bytes through the LD-24 loader's OWN transform _reencode_ocp_to_legacy_halved and the paired scale through _e8m0_to_fp32_doubled. The op therefore consumes the loader's actual output, not a re-derivation of it.

supplementary_cases.name: encoding_field01_odd_mantissa_block
supplementary_cases._role: plan encoding case 2 of 3: a weight block holding bytes at exponent field 0 AND field 1 with ODD mantissas - the halving's entire inexact zone (round-to-nearest-even into the subnormals), so the 2e-05 fp32 clause is actually exercised rather than trivially passed. Constructed by placing the required byte patterns explicitly, then through the same two LD-24 loader transforms.

supplementary_cases.name: activation_group_240_448_and_wide_dynamic_range
supplementary_cases._role: plan encoding case 3 of 3: an activation group whose amax/s would have landed in (240, 448] under the old 448 ceiling - the COMMON case, not a tail case (~90% of ue8m0 groups under a 448 ceiling, assessment section 2.7) - plus a second group carrying more than 13 binades of internal dynamic range. Asserts additionally that no activation byte the op emits carries exponent field 15 on this venue.

supplementary_legs.fallback_vs_plain_torch: same reference callable as above, same clauses
supplementary_legs.simulator_kernel_vs_fallback: same clauses, under the same declared timeout_seconds
supplementary_legs.gate_verdicts: _can_use_block_fp8_linear evaluated on every declared case (harness cases included) and its boolean recorded, so 'the out-of-envelope case took the fallback' is measured rather than assumed

emitted_activation_field15_count._basis: plan section 2 step 0 / R-22: no activation byte this op emits may carry exponent field 15 on trn2, where field 15 is inf/NaN.
